I get what the author is trying to do, but I worry that someone with a REAL need for security (think political dissident in a country with lethal secret police, or a gay person in the many countries where being gay is outlawed and often punishable by death) will think the steps outlined will protect them. It won't.

Data leaks. The smart and dedicated people who this article is trying to defeat are very adept and exploiting these leaks. I don't know enough to tell you all the flaws in the article, but here's two:

  • Awesome, you're using Tails, Tor, and a dynamic MAC address. But you're probably still using the same IP address if you're using your usual Internet connection. So maybe they can't monitor exactly what you're doing, but they do know who you are and where you live. And now you got moved to a list for closer scrutiny.

  • You're encrypting your entire disk. Awesome! Disk encryption is great if your device falls into the wrong hands, and your device was already powered off. But unless you power down after every use, they only have to crack your desktop password. Your desktop has full, unencrypted access to the disk.

The best functional security would be to never use the same device or connection twice. Understood for most people who need such security, this is an impossible goal.
